issues.description: validate_conda uses substring match on --version output, accepting any binary whose output contains 'conda' or 'mamba'.
issues.detail: The check `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ["micromamba", "mamba", "conda"])` admits false positives for arbitrary tools, paths, or output containing those substrings (e.g., 'anaconda-project', '/opt/anaconda/bin/foo'). Match the basename of the executable, or parse the leading token of stdout for an exact identification.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' on the file browser breaks the picker on Linux and macOS.
issues.detail: conda/mamba/micromamba binaries have no extension on non-Windows platforms, so the hardcoded '*.exe' filter shows an empty file picker by default for the majority of users. Either condition the filter on sys.platform or drop it entirely.

issues.description: validate_conda returns True for empty string, conflating 'unset' with 'verified executable'.
issues.detail: Returning True for '' so the preferences page doesn't flag an empty field violates the function's advertised postcondition that the path points to a working conda-like executable. The UI layer should handle 'unset'; the validator should separately answer whether a given path is a real conda binary so callers can trust the contract.

issues.description: run_program(...).communicate() leaks the process handle, with no timeout or returncode check.
issues.detail: The Popen object from run_program is discarded without binding, timeout, or explicit close. A hung or misidentified binary at the user-supplied path will block the UI thread, and live validation on every keystroke can leak file descriptors over a session. Bind the process, set a timeout, and check returncode.

issues.description: setFocus() side effect added to shared create_browsefile helper changes behavior for every other caller.
issues.detail: select_file in widgets/config.py now unconditionally calls edit.setFocus() after picking a file, affecting every preferences page that uses the shared helper, not just the conda field. Make the focus behavior opt-in via parameter, or move the setFocus call into the conda caller.

issues.description: argv() falls back to the user-configured conda path without re-validating at use time.
issues.detail: If find_conda() fails, kernelspec.argv() uses the configured custom_conda path directly. Validation only ran when the preference was entered; nothing guarantees the file still exists, is executable, or is a conda binary when argv() runs. Re-validate at the use site or document that the invariant is not preserved.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a clear NEEDS-WORK verdict: the feature shape is right but the validation layer ships sloppy. Three reviewers independently flag the substring match on --version output and the Windows-only '*.exe' file filter as P1 correctness/portability bugs. Two reviewers flag the empty-string-as-valid lie and the leaked subprocess from run_program. The shared create_browsefile helper grew a setFocus side effect that bleeds into every other caller. Fix validation, platform-gate the filter, scope the focus side effect, and the patch is landable.
